one_liner: Go port of Stream VByte with avo-generated AVX/AVX2 assembly; decodes uint32 arrays 8-14x faster than encoding/binary Uvarint loops.
what_it_does: Encodes and decodes []uint32 in the Stream VByte format (a block of 2-bit length codes followed by the packed data bytes), with optional differential (delta) coding. Two API levels: pkg/stream/writer.WriteAll(in) []byte and reader.ReadAll(count, stream, out), and per-block decode.Get8uint32 / encode.Put8uint32 that take a 16-bit control for 8 values. It is a different format from LEB128, so it replaces Uvarint only where you own both ends; the caller must store the value count separately.
how_it_is_fast: Decoding is a table lookup from each control byte to a PSHUFB mask, then two VPSHUFB shuffles expand 8 packed values into 32 bytes with no per-value branches; delta decoding adds an in-register prefix sum (VPSLLDQ plus VPADDD). Encoding computes control bytes with Lemire's VPMINUB/VPACKUSWB/VPMINSW/VPADDUSW/VPMOVMSKB trick and compacts with VPSHUFB. The assembly is generated with mmcloughlin/avo and chosen at init from golang.org/x/sys/cpu flags (AVX for decode, AVX and AVX2 for encode), with a pure-Go scalar fallback.
when_to_use: Go services on amd64 that store or ship large []uint32 (posting lists, IDs, sorted timestamps as deltas) and control the format.
Bulk decode of thousands to millions of values: README ReadAllFast holds about 5.1-5.7 GB/s from 1e3 to 1e7 values on an i7-8700B.
Sorted inputs with ReadAllDelta/WriteAllDelta, where the deltas fit in 1-2 bytes and the format then compresses.
When you want pure Go plus assembly without cgo bindings to lemire/streamvbyte.
when_not_to_use: You must read or write LEB128/protobuf varints: the format is incompatible; see chmike/varint or dennwc/varint for faster Uvarint.

Non-amd64 targets: by my reading, decode_base.go declares Get8uint32Fast with an int result that does not match the Get8Impl type assigned in decode.go init, and reader_base.go/writer_base.go lack ReadAllDeltaFast/WriteAllDeltaFast, so the packages should not compile on arm64; CI runs only on ubuntu-latest amd64.
Untrusted or externally sized buffers: the assembly ignores slice lengths, so short input or output slices cause silent out-of-bounds reads or writes rather than Go panics.
Production dependency risk: 18 stars, 0 forks, no known importers on pkg.go.dev, last commit 2021-09-12.

integration.dependencies: golang.org/x/sys/cpu; github.com/mmcloughlin/avo (imported by the runtime package pkg/shared via asm.go, not only by the generators); github.com/pkg/errors in go.mod
integration.platforms: amd64 with AVX (decode) and AVX2 (encode) for the fast path; scalar fallback on amd64 without them; other architectures advertised but appear not to build
integration.thread_safety: not documented; functions are stateless apart from read-only lookup tables chosen at init, so concurrent calls on distinct buffers look safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces encoding/binary Uvarint/PutUvarint loops over []uint32 only when you control both encoder and decoder; different wire format and the count must be stored separately

gotchas: Get8uint32Fast/Put8uint32Fast (and the Asm variants) read 16 bytes at in and at in+len(first group), and write 32 bytes to out, without checking len(in) or len(out); pass at least 16 bytes of slack or use the stream API. The scalar versions panic on short slices instead.

ReadAllFast holds back the last 3 control bytes on the assumption that each covers 4 data bytes; by my reading, when count%4==1 and the tail values are 1-byte, the last 16-byte load can run up to 3 bytes past len(stream). It stays inside the allocation for streams from WriteAll (which returns a slice of a 4*count+ctrl buffer), but exactly sized external buffers lack that slack. Not tested here.

Benchmarks use uniform random uint32, so nearly every value takes 4 bytes in Stream VByte and 5 bytes in LEB128: no compression, constant control bytes, and the varint baseline at its slowest length. MB/s counts 4 bytes per decoded integer.
The baseline wrapper util.GetVarint loops on pos < len(data) and ignores Uvarint's n<=0 error return, so truncated input loops forever; it is test scaffolding, not library API.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Use it when you need Stream VByte from Go without cgo; from C or C++ use lemire/streamvbyte (the reference, also catalogued), and if the LEB128 format is fixed use chmike/varint or dennwc/varint instead.
verified_claims_summary: go test -bench output in the README (darwin/amd64, Intel i7-8700B @ 3.20GHz, Go version not stated, go.mod go 1.16): 8-value decode 10095.99 MB/s with AVX versus 731.10 MB/s for an encoding/binary.Uvarint loop (about 13.8x, derived from page data), and stream decode of 1e6 values 5490.62 versus 695.04 MB/s (about 7.9x, derived). The repo's own scalar Stream VByte decoder already reaches about 1659 MB/s, so roughly 2.3x of the gain comes from the format and the rest from SIMD; stream encode gains only about 1.9x (3218.21 vs 1735.08 MB/s at 1e6).
status_note: Abandoned since 2021-09-12 (30 commits, v0.4.0, no open issues, no known importers), Apache-2.0 and small enough to vendor if you add length checks and fix the non-amd64 build.
